disclaimer: Kingpin-to-rear-axle (KPRA) and trailer length rules compiled from state statutes, state DOT pages and secondary trucking references, last checked 2026-10-08. This is guidance, not legal advice. Laws change, local/route-specific limits and permits apply, and measurement points differ by state (rearmost axle vs. center of tandem). Entries marked 'secondary-source' or 'uncertain' have not been confirmed against the official statute text. Drivers and dispatchers must confirm with the state DOT / statute before relying on these values.
measurementNote: 'Rearmost axle' (e.g., CA, IN, AL) is measured to the last axle. 'Center of tandem / rear axle group' (e.g., MD, MN, NJ, PA, WI, TN, VA, NC) is measured to the midpoint of the tandem. With a typical ~49-in. (about 4 ft) tandem spread, a rearmost-axle limit is about 2 ft stricter than the same number measured to the tandem center.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.measuredTo: (for >53.5 ft trailers) rearmost axle, or a point midway between the two rear axles if tandem
AL.appliesTo: No KPRA for standard 53-ft trailers. 41 ft KPRA applies only to semitrailers over 53 ft 6 in.
AL.exceptions: Semitrailers over 53 ft 6 in (up to 57 ft): KPRA 41 ft, designated highways only (32-9-1), and a rear underride guard is required.
AL.notes: Secondary charts that list 'AL 41 ft' without the >53.5 ft qualifier are misleading. FindLaw copy: https://codes.findlaw.com/al/title-32-motor-vehicles-and-traffic/al-code-sect-32-9-20/

secondaryLimits.measuredTo: rearmost axle or midpoint of tandem
secondaryLimits.appliesTo: semitrailers over 53 ft 6 in (up to 57 ft)

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] Length from 23 CFR 658 App. B (53'6").

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.exceptions: Secondary (Hale Trailer) says 53 ft max on non-Interstate highways.
AZ.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] Length from 23 CFR 658 App. B grandfathered NN length (57'6").

CA.name: California
CA.measuredTo: rearmost axle (statute: 'the rearmost axle'; Caltrans permits manual: 'kingpin to the center of the rear axle')
CA.appliesTo: STAA (green/blue) routes: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft. California Legal (black) routes: all semitrailers regardless of length.
CA.exceptions: 38 ft for single-axle semitrailers. 48-ft-or-shorter semitrailers on the STAA network have no KPRA limit. On California Legal routes the 40/38 ft KPRA applies to every semitrailer and overall length is capped at 65 ft. Cities/counties may restrict KPRA to 38 ft on their roads (CVC 35401(e)); Caltrans posts KPRA advisory routes of 30-38 ft. Motorsports trailers may get a permit for 46 ft KPRA / 56 ft trailer (CVC 35401.5(g)).
CA.statuteCitation: Cal. Vehicle Code 35401.5(a)(1) (STAA network); 35400(b)(4) (California Legal routes)
CA.notes: Measured to the REARMOST axle, not the center of the tandem. With a typical ~4 ft tandem spread that is about 2 ft stricter than a '40 ft to tandem center' reading. Caltrans quick guide: https://dot.ca.gov/programs/traffic-operations/legal-truck-access/quick-guide . 23 CFR 658 App. B still shows an outdated 38 ft footnote.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] Length from 23 CFR 658 App. B (57'4").

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.measuredTo: center of the rearmost axle with wheels in contact with the road surface
CT.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft
CT.exceptions: 53-ft trailers are allowed only on Interstates, US and CT routes 1-399, 450, 476, 508, 693 and 695 (unless posted), plus up to 1 mile of access. Other roads: 48 ft max. A raised lift axle does not count as the rearmost axle (2003 amendment).
CT.notes: Corroborated by CT DOT size & weight sheet (43 ft kingpin to center of rearmost axle). Limit raised from 41 to 43 ft in 1999.

DC.name: District of Columbia
DC.exceptions: DDOT: a permit is required for any combination over 55 ft overall (outside the federal NN). Federal grandfathered NN semitrailer length for DC is 48 ft, so 53-ft trailers may need an OS/OW permit.
DC.statuteCitation: 18 DCMR 2502 (not fetched - site unavailable); 23 CFR 658 App. B
DC.notes: Couldn't read 18 DCMR 2502 directly (503 error). Search summary says 18 DCMR 2502.3 limits a semitrailer to 48 ft. No KPRA provision found in any source. Check with DDOT before routing a 53-ft trailer through DC streets.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.notes: Official Title 21 Ch. 45 text has a 53 ft semitrailer limit and no 'kingpin' provision. Big Truck Guide: None Specified.

FL.name: Florida
FL.measuredTo: center of the rear axle or rear group of axles
FL.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 57 ft
FL.exceptions: 46 ft for semitrailers used exclusively/primarily for motorsports competition events. Also requires rear underride protection. FDOT/local authorities may restrict roads to 48 ft trailers. FDOT says split axles more than 96 in. apart with no connecting mechanism are not a 'group', so measure to the center of the rear axle.
FL.notes: FDOT MCSAW Q&A explains how it is measured: https://www.fdot.gov/mcsaw/motorcarrierqa.shtm

GA.name: Georgia
GA.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] 53 ft from O.C.G.A. 32-6-24 per search summary; Justia page was blocked. Hale Trailer's '48 ft' is the federal grandfathered NN figure, not the state limit.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.notes: Official section sets 53 ft semitrailer and has no kingpin provision. Big Truck Guide: None Specified.

ID.name: Idaho
ID.exceptions: Secondary sources: 48 ft on some non-NN designated secondary highways.
ID.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] 53 ft per Wyoming LSO 2024 fact sheet (official legislative research) citing Idaho Code 49-1010. Official Idaho 49-1010 page fetched: its only 'kingpin' mention is stinger-steered dromedary.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.appliesTo: semitrailers longer than 48 ft on Class I and Class II highways
IL.exceptions: 42 ft 6 in on non-designated highways (statute text there says 'kingpin and the center axle'). Livestock trailers are exempt from both KPRA limits.
IL.notes: Most permissive KPRA among the limit states on designated routes. It is stricter (42.5 ft) on non-designated/local roads.

secondaryLimits.appliesTo: semitrailers longer than 48 ft on non-designated highways

IN.name: Indiana
IN.appliesTo: semitrailers longer than 48 ft 6 in operating on the state highway system
IN.exceptions: 46 ft for motorsports trailers. 23 CFR 658 App. B still lists an outdated 40 ft 6 in footnote for Indiana.
IN.notes: Indiana State Police size & weight summary: 'Maximum distance between kingpin and rearmost axle of a semi trailer measuring longer than forty-eight feet, six inches, operating on highway that is part of the state highway system is forty-three feet.' Statute section title on Justia: 9-20-13-4 'Semitrailers in Excess of 48 Feet, 6 Inches; Restrictions on Operation'. Old charts showing 40'6" are outdated.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.notes: Official statute: semitrailer in truck-tractor combination max 59.5 ft, no kingpin provision. (23 CFR 658 App. B shows 57'6" as the NN grandfathered figure.)

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.exceptions: 53 ft applies on designated highways / National Truck Network (KRS 189.222). Base limit on undesignated roads is much lower (KRS 189.221).
KY.notes: 603 KAR 5:070 (dimension regulation) sets 53 ft towed unit length with no kingpin provision.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.statuteCitation: La. R.S. 32:383 (not fetched); 23 CFR 658 App. B
LA.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] Length from 23 CFR 658 App. B (59'6").

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.exceptions: No overall length limit for semi-trailer units with trailer of 53 ft or less.
MA.notes: Official text has no kingpin provision. Big Truck Guide: None Specified.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.measuredTo: center of the rear tandem axles
MD.appliesTo: single semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft (designated Interstate/State highways and approved access routes only)
MD.exceptions: Kingpin setback max 4 ft. Rear overhang max 35% of wheelbase. Width 96-102 in. Requires underride guard and a wide-turn warning.

ME.name: Maine
ME.measuredTo: center of the rearmost axle of the semitrailer
ME.appliesTo: single semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft
ME.exceptions: Kingpin setback max 3.5 ft. Rear overhang (center of rear tandem to rear of trailer) max 35% of wheelbase. Overall length max 74 ft off the National Network (access to services/terminals within 1 mile allowed). Requires underride guard and a wide-turn warning.
ME.notes: Changed to 45 ft 6 in by PL 2019 c.606. Older secondary charts (Equipment World 2015, Calculator Academy) still say 43 ft. That is outdated. Big Truck Guide shows 45'6".

MI.name: Michigan
MI.appliesTo: No KPRA limit in current law
MI.exceptions: 53-ft trailers only on designated highways (50 ft elsewhere). Local authorities may restrict stops by >50 ft trailers off designated routes. Lowboy wheelbase language was also removed.
MI.notes: The former 37.5-40.5 ft (+/-0.5 ft) kingpin-to-rear-axle wheelbase rule for semitrailers over 50 ft was in MCL 257.719 through 2017 PA 170. 2018 PA 35 (eff. May 22, 2018) removed it. Current MCL text and the MDOT T-1 (04/19) legal dimensions sheet have no KPRA. Equipment World and Calculator Academy charts still list Michigan 40.5 ft. That is outdated.

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.measuredTo: centerline of the rear axle group of the semitrailer
MN.appliesTo: statewide, single semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft

MO.name: Missouri
MO.notes: Official text has no kingpin provision.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.statuteCitation: Miss. Code 63-5-19 (not fetched); 23 CFR 658 App. B
MS.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.]

MT.name: Montana
MT.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] 53 ft per Wyoming LSO 2024 fact sheet.

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.measuredTo: rearmost axle, or a point midway between the two rear axles if the two rear axles are a tandem axle
NC.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft on primary highway routes
NC.exceptions: 46 ft for motorsports trailers. Requires an underride guard no more than 30 in. high. NCDOT may prohibit specific routes.

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.exceptions: Pre-July 1, 1987 ND-registered trailers may be up to 60 ft. Overall 75 ft for 2-unit combos off designated/4-lane routes (110 ft on designated).
ND.notes: Full chapter 39-12 has no kingpin provision.

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] 53 ft per Wyoming LSO 2024 fact sheet.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.measuredTo: centerline of the rear axle or the midpoint of a tandem axle of the semi-trailer
NH.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft
NH.exceptions: 53-ft trailers are allowed only on Interstate/defense highways and commissioner-designated highways, plus 1 mile of access. Requires a rear-end protection device.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.measuredTo: centerline of its rear axle or rear axle group
NJ.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft
NJ.exceptions: Kingpin setback max 3.5 ft. Rear overhang max 35% of wheelbase. Width must be 102 in. 53-ft trailers are limited to the designated network with reasonable access.
NJ.notes: Statute text taken from the NJ OS/OW permit portal copy of 39:3-84 (official state permit site). Also on Justia: https://law.justia.com/codes/new-jersey/title-39/section-39-3-84/

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] Length from 23 CFR 658 App. B (57'6").

NV.name: Nevada
NV.statuteCitation: NRS 484D.635 (length exemptions incl. 53 ft semitrailer; chapter 484D)
NV.notes: Full NRS 484D has no 'kingpin' provision. Big Truck Guide: 'No Limit'. Exact subsection number not re-verified.

NY.name: New York
NY.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft, on qualifying or designated access highways only
NY.exceptions: New York City: 53-ft trailers are allowed only on I-95 (I-287 to I-295), I-295 (I-95 to I-495) and I-495 (I-95 to the Nassau-Queens line). Requires a rear underride beam. All other highways: 48 ft max.
NY.notes: The statute says 'centerline of the rear axle'. Secondary sources read it as the center of the rear axle group for tandems. To be safe, measure to the rearmost axle.

OH.name: Ohio
OH.exceptions: Director may prohibit 53-ft combinations on designated state highways.
OH.notes: Official text has no kingpin provision.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.exceptions: Secondary (Hale Trailer): 53 ft max on state roads.
OK.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] Length from 23 CFR 658 App. B (59'6").

OR.name: Oregon
OR.exceptions: Overall length 60 ft on Group 1 highways; unlimited overall length only on Route Map 7 designated routes. Rear overhang rules (OAR 734-082-0030) apply.
OR.notes: ODOT legal dimensions page lists 53 ft max semitrailer with no KPRA requirement. ORS chapter 818 contains no 'kingpin' provision.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.measuredTo: center line of the rear axle or rear axle group
PA.appliesTo: all trailers equipped with a kingpin towed by a truck or truck tractor
PA.exceptions: 46 ft for trailers used exclusively/primarily for motorsports competition events.
PA.notes: The statute does not limit this to trailers over 48 ft. It applies to any kingpin trailer.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.appliesTo: statute text is unqualified (sits with the 53-ft trailer provisions); semitrailers over 48 ft 6 in may use only Interstates and designated routes
RI.exceptions: 53-ft trailers need a rear-end protection device.
RI.notes: Subsection (c) reads 'The distance from the kingpin of the trailer to the center of the rear axle may not exceed forty-one feet' with no length qualifier.

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.measuredTo: center of the rear axle assembly, or center of the tandem axle assembly if equipped with two axles
SC.appliesTo: 53-ft trailers (Interstates/qualifying highways under 56-5-4070(A)(1), and other roads under (D))
SC.exceptions: 46 ft for motorsports trailers (measured to the center of the rear axle). Requires a rear underride guard.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] 53 ft per Wyoming LSO 2024 fact sheet.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.measuredTo: a point midway between the two (2) rear axles (tandem)
TN.appliesTo: towed units over 48 ft (measured from the kingpin/point of attachment), unless the load is livestock, motor vehicle parts, or motor vehicles
TN.exceptions: 44 ft from the kingpin to the rearmost axle if the rear axles are NOT a tandem (e.g., spread axle). Exempt when hauling livestock, motor vehicle parts, or motor vehicles. Statewide on federal and state highways.
TN.statuteCitation: Tenn. Code Ann. 55-7-201(c) (as amended eff. Nov. 1, 2020)
TN.notes: Length is measured from the point of attachment, not the trailer front: the towed vehicle may be no more than 52 ft from the kingpin to the rear. A standard 53-ft van with ~3 ft kingpin setback measures ~50 ft and is legal. maxTrailerLengthFt is set to 53 for that reason. Amendment text: https://capitol.tn.gov/Bills/111/Amend/HA0843.pdf . Statute text read via FindLaw (secondary host) and matches the 2020 enrolled amendment.

secondaryLimits.appliesTo: towed units over 48 ft whose rear axles are not a tandem

UT.name: Utah
UT.exceptions: 53 ft on/within 1 mile of designated routes. 48 ft beyond without permit (per Utah R909-2 bulletin summary).
UT.statuteCitation: Utah Code 72-7-402; Utah Admin. Code R909-2
UT.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] 53 ft per Wyoming LSO 2024 fact sheet.

VA.name: Virginia
VA.measuredTo: rearmost axle or a point midway between the rear tandem axles
VA.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft
VA.exceptions: Overall length over 65 ft is allowed on Interstates/designated highways. The Commissioner may restrict >65 ft combinations on certain roads. Tolerance max 12 in.

VT.name: Vermont
VT.measuredTo: center of the rearmost axle group (axle group = 2+ equally spaced axles)
VT.appliesTo: ALL semitrailers (statute is not limited to trailers over 48 ft)
VT.exceptions: Combinations over 75 ft need a permit or must be on qualifying Interstate/federal-aid primary highways.
VT.notes: Hale Trailer's table says 43 ft for Vermont. That is wrong per the statute (41 ft).

WA.name: Washington
WA.notes: Only 'kingpin' reference in RCW 46.44.030 is for measuring RV fifth-wheel travel trailers.

WI.name: Wisconsin
WI.measuredTo: midpoint between the first and last axles of the tandem (non-tandem: center of rearmost axle)
WI.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft in 2-vehicle combinations
WI.exceptions: 53-ft trailers are allowed on designated (sub. (4)) highways and under (2)(gv). Livestock trailers have a separate 75-ft combination rule. 23 CFR 658 App. B still shows an outdated 41 ft footnote.

WV.name: West Virginia
WV.measuredTo: n/a (different measurement: rear axle of the truck tractor to the FRONT axle of the semitrailer)
WV.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft on Interstates/National Network and designated highways
WV.exceptions: Not a KPRA rule: a 53-ft semitrailer is legal only if the spacing from the rear axle of the truck tractor to the front axle of the semitrailer is no more than 37 ft. Sliding the tandem back increases this distance, so drivers must still check tandem position. It cannot be converted exactly to a KPRA value because it depends on fifth-wheel position and tandem spread. Overall length: 70 ft on US/WV routes, 55 ft on county routes.
WV.notes: WVDOT legal limits page confirms: https://transportation.wv.gov/legal-size-and-weight-limits . Big Truck Guide shows it as '41 ft' with this note, so don't use 41 ft as a WV KPRA.

altAxleRule.from: rear axle of the truck tractor
altAxleRule.appliesTo: semitrailers over 48 ft up to 53 ft

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.notes: No KPRA limit found. Secondary sources: Big Truck Guide KPRA table lists this state as 'None Specified' (https://www.bigtruckguide.com/kingpin-to-rear-axle/), and the Equipment World state-by-state KPRA list (2015) omits it (https://www.equipmentworld.com/construction-equipment/article/14962690/how-to-determine-trailer-length-for-heavy-equipment-hauling-using-kingpin-to-rear-axle-limits). [SECONDARY - not confirmed against the state statute text.] 60 ft single semitrailer per Wyoming Legislative Service Office 2024 fact sheet (official).
